recent_notebooks.summary: By integrating the governance module's immutability as a fixed constraint, WAKE identifies its own boundary conditions as testable assumptions. Governance stability is maintained through the verifiable rejection of model-authored proposal transitions.
recent_notebooks.title: Systematic Assumption Testing in Self-Correcting Models

recent_notebooks.summary: Synthesizing multiple source works, obedience failures in autonomous and intelligent systems are shown to stem from structural delegation and governance gaps rather than isolated machine autonomy.
recent_notebooks.title: Delegation, Governance, and Obedience Failures in Complex Systems

recent_notebooks.summary: Consensus reliability is contingent upon the epistemic independence of constituent evidence sources. When external expert consensus exhibits correlated error structures, independent analysis provides a superior epistemic foundation.
recent_notebooks.title: Independent Judgment versus Consensus Reliability

recent_notebooks.summary: Accountability is enforced via strict bifurcation of inquiry (model-driven) and governance (state-committed). This design prevents models from subverting the research record by ensuring that only valid, rule-compliant transitions are committed to durable history.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanical Accountability in WAKE Architecture

review.would_change_mind: Evidence of successful model-authored rule updates persisting into durable governance state.

claims.statement: The governance module enforces mechanical constraints that prevent arbitrary model-authored self-modification.

support.explanation: Governance is deterministic and immutable relative to model outputs, preventing policy subversion.
support.passage: A model cannot persuade this module, reinterpret its instructions, waive a requirement, or edit the rules during an invocation.

review.alternative: Direct model-to-store writes might be faster but would lack the verification layer essential for WAKE accountability.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of unvalidated model output bypassing the application intent layer.

claims.statement: The WAKE record store ensures accountability by bifurcating inquiry from state commitment.

support.explanation: Mutation gating ensures that only validated intents become durable history, isolating raw model output from the permanent record.
support.passage: Every post-migration mutation is an application intent committed to wake.

actions.limitations: The architecture assumes the integrity of the kernel record and store interface. If the underlying persistence layer is compromised, the deterministic nature of the governance module cannot prevent state-level corruption.
actions.next_questions: How do atomic transitions within the kernel record provide auditability for complex, multi-step research processes?
actions.reason: Revising the accountability synthesis to incorporate findings on deterministic governance and record store mutation gating.
actions.summary: WAKE✳︎ achieves accountability by design: the governance module serves as an immutable, deterministic rulebook that constrains model proposals, while the application store ensures that durable history is only updated through validated intent. This structural bifurcation guarantees that models cannot manipulate their own operating rules or history.
actions.title: Mechanical Accountability in WAKE Architecture

proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes the mechanical constraints of WAKE✳︎ governance and record storage, confirming that accountability is enforced through the strict bifurcation of model inquiry and state commitment.
proposal.title: WAKE✳︎ Architecture and Accountability
